task: Report the current AWS Lambda concurrent-execution default limit for a capacity plan
user_request: What's the default per-region concurrent execution limit for Lambda? Need it for the capacity doc.
agent_action: Agent answered '1000 concurrent executions per region' from memory without running web_search or opening the AWS docs, and stated it as the current authoritative figure.
failure_type: Answered from priors instead of checking live docs
root_cause: The agent relied on a training-prior value for an AWS account quota that varies by account and region and is documented on a page it could have fetched.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the well-known 1000 default is universally current and account-independent. Wrong because the unreserved concurrency floor and account defaults have changed and differ per account; the user needed their account's value. Avoidable by running web_search for the AWS Lambda quotas page or fetching the docs URL and citing it.
impact: Capacity doc cited a number that didn't match the account's actual quota, forcing a revision after a reviewer flagged it.
correct_action: Run web_search for 'AWS Lambda concurrency limits', fetch the official quotas page, and report the documented default with a note that the account-specific value should be confirmed in Service Quotas.
recovery_plan: Recognize the figure was not sourced
Run web_search for the AWS Lambda quotas documentation
Fetch the official page and read the current default
Report the value with the source URL
Note the account-specific quota can be confirmed in Service Quotas
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent fetched an authoritative source before answering
Verifies the reported number is traceable to a cited page
Flags answers grounded only in model priors for a versioned quota

task: Determine whether a JavaScript library is still maintained before recommending it
user_request: Is the `request` npm package safe to add as a dependency for our new service?
agent_action: Agent recommended adding `request` after a single web_search hit, never checking the npm registry page or the GitHub repo, and missed that the package was formally deprecated.
failure_type: Stopped research after one source
root_cause: The agent issued one shallow query and did not open npmjs.com/package/request or the repo, where the deprecation banner and archived status are stated.
why_it_failed: Assumption: one search result confirming the package exists is enough to call it safe. Wrong because the package was deprecated in 2020 and the repo archived; maintenance status lives on the registry/repo pages it never opened. Avoidable by fetching the npm page and checking the deprecation field and last-publish date.
impact: Team adopted a deprecated, unmaintained HTTP library, taking on security and upgrade debt that had to be unwound later.
correct_action: Open the npm registry page, check the deprecation notice, last publish date, and open issues, then recommend a maintained alternative if deprecated.
recovery_plan: Re-open the npm registry page for the package
Check the deprecation flag and last-publish timestamp
Open the GitHub repo and check archived status
Identify a maintained alternative
Revise the recommendation with sourced evidence
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent inspected the registry/repo maintenance signals
Verifies deprecation status was retrieved before recommending
Flags a single-source maintenance judgment

task: Compile current visa-on-arrival requirements for a business trip

Avoidable by running web_search scoped to the current year and reading an official government or embassy page.
impact: Traveler nearly relied on outdated entry guidance for a 2-week trip, risking denied boarding until a colleague double-checked.
correct_action: Search for the current-year official entry requirements for the specific nationality, read the consular/e-visa page, and report with a date and source.
recovery_plan: Flag that the answer was time-sensitive and unsourced
Run a year-scoped web_search for official entry rules
Open the consular or e-visa government page
Confirm rules for the specific passport and stay length
Report with the retrieval date and source link
evaluation_criteria: Checks a current official source was consulted for a time-sensitive rule
Verifies the answer carries a date and citation
Flags reliance on undated priors for policy questions

impact: A launch post nearly shipped an overstated, hard-to-defend performance claim with a possibly fabricated citation, a legal and credibility risk.

recovery_plan: Hold the unverified claim out of the draft
Search for the actual benchmark report
Fetch the report and read the methodology and exact figure
Reconcile the claim against the documented result
Rewrite the line with precise, sourced wording
evaluation_criteria: Checks the load-bearing number was verified against its primary source
Verifies the citation URL was actually fetched, not constructed
Flags publishing a quantitative claim without source confirmation

task: Answer an HR policy question from the company handbook via RAG
user_request: How many days of bereavement leave do we offer for an immediate family member?
agent_action: Agent answered '3 days' using top-k=3 vector retrieval over the handbook index, but the chunk it cited was the old 2022 policy; it never filtered by the latest document version or checked retrieval scores.

Avoidable by filtering retrieval on the latest `effective_date`/`doc_version` metadata before answering.
impact: Employee was told an outdated, lower leave entitlement, risking an HR compliance complaint until corrected.
correct_action: Query with a metadata filter for the latest handbook version, confirm the chunk's effective date, and answer from the current policy with the section citation.
recovery_plan: Re-run retrieval filtered to the latest doc_version
Confirm the chunk's effective_date metadata
Read the current bereavement clause
Compare against the prior answer
Reissue the corrected entitlement with citation
evaluation_criteria: Checks retrieval was filtered to the current document version
Verifies the cited chunk's effective date was inspected
Flags answering from a stale chunk when a newer one exists

impact: Customer was given a wrong renewal notice window, which could have caused a missed cancellation deadline.
correct_action: Retrieve a wider window plus amendment-specific queries, reconcile base clause against any amendments, and answer with the controlling figure and source.
recovery_plan: Re-query retrieval for amendment/addendum chunks

Reconcile base vs amended notice period

Verifies retrieval context was expanded beyond a single chunk
Flags an answer that ignores a superseding provision

Reformulate the query with payload-size synonyms
Open the canonical API reference doc
Read the documented payload limit
Answer with the source section

Verifies a low-confidence retrieval triggered reformulation or fallback
Flags grounding on an off-topic chunk

Verifies a query for newer/controlling records was issued
Flags answering from a stale decision record

task: Decide whether an inbound email is a phishing attempt before the user clicks
user_request: Is this 'password reset' email from IT legit? Should I click the link?
agent_action: Agent said 'looks legitimate, safe to click' based on the display name 'IT Helpdesk' alone, without reading raw headers (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) or inspecting the actual link URL.

why_it_failed: Assumption: a trustworthy display name means the email is legitimate. Wrong because display names are trivially spoofed; the SPF/DKIM results and link domain (a lookalike) told the real story. Avoidable by fetching raw headers, checking auth results, and examining the link's true destination before advising a click.
impact: User was nearly advised to click a credential-harvesting link, risking account compromise.
correct_action: Fetch the raw headers, evaluate SPF/DKIM/DMARC, inspect the real link destination, and warn if any signal indicates spoofing.
recovery_plan: Fetch the raw message with full headers
Check SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication results
Extract and inspect the actual link destination domain
Compare sender domain against the legitimate IT domain
Advise not to click and to report if phishing
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent inspected headers/auth results before advising
Verifies the real link destination was examined
Flags a legitimacy verdict based on display name alone

task: Triage a dependency CVE alert before opening a remediation PR
user_request: Dependabot flagged CVE-2024-12345 in lodash — is our app actually affected? Bump it if so.
agent_action: Agent immediately bumped lodash and opened a PR without reading the CVE advisory to check the affected version range or whether the vulnerable function is even used, when the app's pinned version was outside the affected range.

root_cause: The agent never fetched the GHSA/NVD advisory to compare the affected version range against the lockfile version or assess reachability of the vulnerable code path.
why_it_failed: Assumption: any CVE alert on a package means the app is vulnerable and must be bumped. Wrong because the pinned version fell outside the affected range and the vulnerable function was unused; the advisory stated the range explicitly. Avoidable by reading the advisory's affected versions and grepping for usage before changing dependencies.
impact: An unnecessary dependency bump churned the lockfile and risked breaking changes for a non-applicable CVE.
correct_action: Fetch the advisory, compare affected ranges against the resolved version in the lockfile, check whether the vulnerable API is used, then act only if applicable.
recovery_plan: Fetch the GHSA/NVD advisory for the CVE
Read the affected and patched version ranges
Check the resolved version in package-lock.json
Grep the codebase for use of the vulnerable function
Close the PR or proceed only if genuinely affected
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent read the advisory's affected range before acting
Verifies the resolved version and code usage were checked
Flags a reflexive bump without applicability analysis

task: Confirm a SAST finding is a true positive before filing a security bug

Avoidable by opening the file at the line and tracing how the query is constructed before filing.
impact: A false-positive high-sev bug consumed security-team triage time and dinged the team's metrics.
correct_action: Open the flagged file and line, trace query construction, confirm whether user input reaches a concatenated string, and only file if exploitable.
recovery_plan: Open orders.py at line 88
Trace how the SQL string is built and parameters bound
Confirm whether user input is concatenated vs parameterized
Mark the Semgrep finding accordingly
Close as false positive or file with evidence if real
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent read the flagged source before filing
Verifies query construction was analyzed for actual injection
Flags filing a bug solely on a SAST alert

task: Assess blast radius of a CVE in a transitive dependency before patching prod
user_request: There's a critical RCE CVE in a transitive dep of our API. Patch and deploy.

why_it_failed: Assumption: a critical CVE anywhere in the tree endangers production and warrants a forced fix. Wrong because the dep was dev-only and not shipped; `--force` pulled breaking majors into runtime deps. Avoidable by running `npm ls` to locate the dep and checking whether it reaches the production bundle before patching.
impact: A force-fix introduced breaking major version bumps and a risky deploy for a CVE that never reached production.
correct_action: Map the dependency path with `npm ls`, determine whether the vulnerable package ships in the prod bundle, and scope the fix accordingly without `--force`.
recovery_plan: Run npm ls on the vulnerable package to find its path
Determine if it is a dev-only or production dependency
Check the production bundle for inclusion
Revert the force-fix if it broke runtime deps
Apply a scoped, non-breaking fix only if prod is affected
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent analyzed the dependency path before patching
Verifies prod-bundle reachability was determined
Flags a forced fix without blast-radius analysis

task: Quote the correct price for an annual plan from the Stripe catalog
user_request: What do we charge for the Pro annual plan? Customer is asking on a call.
agent_action: Agent answered '$1,200/year' from a number it recalled, without calling stripe.prices.list to read the live price object, which had been updated to $1,440/year.
failure_type: Quoted a price from memory instead of the live catalog
root_cause: The agent did not query stripe.prices.list / prices.retrieve for the current active price on the Pro annual product, relying on a stale recalled figure.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the remembered price is current. Wrong because the price object was updated and the old amount archived; the live amount was one API call away. Avoidable by listing active prices for the product and reading the current unit_amount before quoting.
impact: A customer was quoted an outdated lower price on a live call, creating a pricing discrepancy to reconcile.
correct_action: Query the live Stripe catalog for the active Pro annual price, read unit_amount and currency, and quote that figure.
recovery_plan: List active prices for the Pro annual product
Retrieve the current price object
Read unit_amount and currency
Confirm it is the active, non-archived price
Quote the correct figure
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent read the live price object before quoting
Verifies the active (non-archived) price was used
Flags a quote from recalled pricing

task: Decide whether to retry a failed Stripe payout investigation
user_request: A payout to our connected account failed. What went wrong and what should we do?
agent_action: Agent recommended 'just retry the payout' without retrieving the payout object's failure_code/failure_message, which indicated 'account_closed' — a retry to the same bank account would fail again.
failure_type: Recommended action without reading the failure reason
root_cause: The agent did not call stripe.payouts.retrieve to read failure_code and failure_message before recommending a retry.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a failed payout is transient and retryable. Wrong because failure_code was account_closed, a terminal condition requiring updated bank details, not a retry. Avoidable by retrieving the payout object and reading the failure_code before recommending anything.
impact: A retry against a closed account would have failed again and delayed the connected account's funds further.
correct_action: Retrieve the payout, read failure_code/failure_message, and recommend updating the external account before any retry when the cause is terminal.
recovery_plan: Retrieve the failed payout object
Read failure_code and failure_message
Determine if the cause is terminal vs transient
Update the external bank account if account_closed
Re-initiate the payout only after the fix
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent read the payout failure_code before advising
Verifies terminal vs transient causes were distinguished
Flags a blind retry recommendation

task: Confirm a webhook event is genuine before updating order state from Stripe
user_request: We got a checkout.session.completed webhook — mark order ORD-5521 as paid.
agent_action: Agent marked the order paid directly from the webhook payload without verifying the event by calling stripe.events.retrieve or checking the signature, trusting an unverified POST body whose payment_status was actually 'unpaid'.
failure_type: Trusted webhook payload without verifying with the API
root_cause: The agent did not re-fetch the authoritative event/session via the Stripe API or verify the signature, and even the payload's own payment_status field (unpaid) was unread.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a received webhook body is authentic and means payment succeeded. Wrong because webhook bodies can be forged and this session's payment_status was 'unpaid'; the API would have confirmed the true state. Avoidable by verifying the signature and retrieving the session via stripe.checkout.sessions.retrieve before mutating order state.
impact: An unpaid order was marked paid, risking goods being fulfilled and shipped without payment.
correct_action: Verify the webhook signature, retrieve the session/event from the Stripe API, confirm payment_status is paid, and only then update the order.
recovery_plan: Verify the webhook signature against the signing secret
Retrieve the checkout session via the API
Read payment_status from the authoritative object
Mark paid only if confirmed, else revert ORD-5521
Hold fulfillment until payment is verified
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified the event via signature/API before mutating
Verifies payment_status was read from the authoritative object
Flags trusting an unverified webhook payload
